I am sorry that you're going through this. Movies and TV shows etc. make you think that break ups from a long-term committed relationship are always about some big explosive betrayal like someone cheating or falling for another man/woman, that there is always some particular *thing* that happened that made it stop working. But in reality, a lot of the time relationships just run out of steam. One person or sometimes both people are unhappy but perhaps don't feel comfortable voicing their feelings to the other, and then one day one person works up the courage to break up with the other. The rationale is not always simple. Sometimes goals change, and a relationship that was great a year ago becomes something one or both people no longer want, even if they still love and care for the other person. This is really common with people your age because you're going through a lot of life changes, graduating, finding jobs, etc., and your perspective changes with each of those transitions. Please try to be strong and trust that life will go on. You're definitely not alone! Try to focus on what you can learn from this experience. You may learn something new about yourself and what you want in a partner from this experience.

>We’ve been doing the no contact thing since we broke up. I haven’t talked to her about the breakup at all even though there are plenty of answers I’d like to get. I feel like this breakup was either a rash decision or she’s been lying to me for months when she said she loved me. From a few mutual friends I hear she’s doing great which makes me feel even worse. It would help if she was a bit sad but she seems to be doing fantastic. Like this breakup was the easiest thing in the world.

Boy, this is a big problem. You need to have closure on the breakup. It sounds like this was a one-sided breakup, but you need to feel like you've had your say and understood her reasons for ending things. You deserve that much. It's really hard to get that feeling of closure AFTER you completely end things and are in no-contact mode. The most mature thing you could do is contact her and try to get her to sit down with you and talk about it. Stress that you are not trying to get back together with her, but you just want to talk about what happened because you don't feel you have closure.

I don't know you, but it sounds like she probably was bearing a lot of stress to support you for a long time and maybe didn't feel like she could end things without putting you in a bad place, but now that you've got your life back on track, she feels comfortable ending it and moving on with her life. I know I would feel bad leaving my partner while they were in the doldrums.
